eligibility_rationale: Floral morphology is associated with robbery susceptibility, but the source does not estimate a matching pollinator response to the same morphological coordinate; robbery-state effects on hawkmoth visitation do not create a paired trait geometry.

Xylocopa latipes can act as both primary nectar robber and legitimate pollinator, while robbed-flower state changes foraging behaviour. Functional sign is consumer-state dependent rather than a fixed antagonist response to a plant trait axis.

Manual nectar robbing changes pollinator foraging and fruit set, but robbery intensity is the imposed interaction state rather than an independently declared floral trait coordinate with two functional responses.

Elevation structures legitimate visitation, nectar robbery and seed production, but the study does not isolate one plant trait coordinate receiving both functional responses. Retain as spatial interaction-context evidence.
